title: stark scale europes wildfires 2026 07 31
text:
What happened this week
Wildfires continued to rage across an increasingly tinder-dry Europe, which is now the world's fastest-warming continent.
By Thursday, France and Spain saw some relief from fires that have forced large-scale evacuations. Greek firefighters battled deadly blazes on the island of Crete for a second day. In eastern England, a wildfire forced evacuations of nearby communities, bringing scenes more commonly associated with southern Europe.
What the numbers show
The amount of land burned in France helps show how severe this year's fires have been: Wildfires there have burned more than 90,000 hectares so far this year, close to double the record for the same time of year from 2006 to 2025.
More than 200,000 hectares have burned in Spain this year, far more than average.
What's next
Thursday's temperatures showed that Europe was the furthest from its historical norm of any continent by a wide margin; you can check the Reuters Climate Monitor to keep tracking heatwaves like the one in Western Europe.
